name: Python
description: From your very first line of code to building your own programming language. Lessons, real tools, puzzles and bosses.

errors.IndexError: You asked for a position in a list (or string) that doesn't exist, like item [1] of a list with only 1 thing in it. Check how long it really is: print it with repr().
errors.KeyError: You looked up a key in a dict that isn't there. Use `key in d` to check first, or d.get(key, default).
errors.NameError: Python doesn't know that name. Usually a typo, or a variable used before it was created, or an import you forgot.
errors.TypeError: You used a value the wrong way: adding a number to a string, calling something that isn't a function, or passing the wrong number of arguments.
errors.AttributeError: That object doesn't have that method or attribute. Check the spelling, and check what type it really is with type(x).
errors.ValueError: Right type, wrong value, like int("hello"). The value can't be used the way you tried.
errors.SyntaxError: Python couldn't even read the file. Look for a missing colon, bracket, or quote on that line or the line above it.
errors.IndentationError: The spaces at the start of a line don't line up. Everything inside the same block needs the same indentation.
errors.UnboundLocalError: You used a variable inside a function before giving it a value in that function.
errors.RecursionError: A function called itself too many times (Python stops at about 1000 levels deep). Either it never stops, or the problem needs a loop instead of recursion.
errors.ZeroDivisionError: You divided by zero. Check for that case before dividing.
errors.FileNotFoundError: That file path doesn't exist. Print the path you're opening and check it, especially relative paths.
errors.ModuleNotFoundError: Python can't find that module. Check the spelling of the import.
errors.ImportError: The import failed. Check the names you're importing actually exist in that module.
errors.AssertionError: An assert in your own code failed.
